gap: No result ChatGPT got works out what each NAS's recognition features can actually do with the RAM it ships with. The Synology DS225+ and DS425+ come with 2 GB. That is half of the 4 GB Synology needs for object recognition, and Immich needs 6 GB to run face recognition and smart search at all. The only fix is adding one 4 GB module, which brings the box to 6 GB: Immich's minimum, not its 8 GB recommendation. Synology says non-Synology memory voids full warranty and technical support coverage.
standout_why: I compared this against the pages ChatGPT cited and the top results. The Synology compare page (cited) has the footnote 'Object recognition requires an upgrade of memory capacity to a minimum of 4 GB' for DS225+/DS425+, but nothing about Immich. esp32.co.uk (cited) gives Immich's '6 GB minimum, 8 GB recommended' but no model's shipped RAM; it only says 'Check exact Synology model'. homelabcompass.com (cited) gives no RAM figures, only that Immich ML 'wants some headroom'. The Synology Photos tech spec (cited) has no RAM figure. needtoknowit.com.au (not in ChatGPT's results) covers the Synology 4 GB rule, but nothing about Immich's needs. None of these pages puts each box's shipped RAM next to both apps' thresholds. None says that Immich with only 4 GB means machine learning is turned off, so there is no face recognition or smart search. None mentions the warranty condition on non-Synology RAM.
decides: This confirms Synology DS225+/DS425+ for families who stay on Synology Photos and add Synology's 4 GB module. It rules them out for the 'NAS + Immich' route ChatGPT offers as the closer Google Photos copy: even fully upgraded they reach only 6 GB, Immich's floor. For Immich, pick a box that ships with 8 GB or more, such as the UGREEN DH4300 Plus (8 GB fixed) or QNAP TS-264-8G (8 GB), or upgrade a DS925+, which ships with 4 GB and takes up to 32 GB. The DH2300's 4 GB can run Immich only with machine learning disabled.
